also: your ears are full of wax

terms.gloss: the dirt of the ears: earwax
terms.grammar: sordēs, sordium f. pl., with the genitive aurium; singular sordēs, sordis f., ablative sorde
evidence: Cic. ND 2.144: in sordibus aurium tamquam in viscō inhaerēsceret
Hor. Ep. 1.2.53: auriculās … collēctā sorde dolentīs
terms.comment: Cicero’s phrase for the wax in which any tiny creature that tries to get into the ear sticks, as in birdlime. Horace has the singular, of ears that ache with wax that has built up.

phrases.latin: Aurēs tibi pūrgābō: sordium plēnae sunt.
phrases.english: I’ll clean your ears: they’re full of wax.

phrases.latin: prōvīsum etiam, ut, sī qua minima bēstiola cōnārētur inrumpere, in sordibus aurium tamquam in viscō inhaerēsceret
phrases.english: care was even taken that if any tiny creature tried to force its way in, it would stick in the wax of the ears as if in birdlime

phrases.latin: ut lippum pictae tabulae, fōmenta podagram, auriculās citharae collēctā sorde dolentīs
phrases.english: as painted pictures please a man with sore eyes, warm compresses the gout, and the lyre ears that ache with built-up wax

sources: Lewis & Short: sordes · Lewis & Short: auris
